title: Renewal KPI Field Guide — Performance & Cost
content:
Purpose:
This working guide distills the minimum viable metric definitions and a compact KPI table for renewal conversations focused on inference performance and unit economics. It’s aimed at CS managers and solutions engineers who need crisp, comparable signals to use in QBRs and renewal playbooks.

What’s different about this doc:
- Focus on metric definitions that map directly to engineering observability (Prometheus/logs) and billing data so CS can quickly validate customer concerns.
- Lightweight action thresholds and recommended owners for each KPI.
- Compact CSV-style KPI table that can be copy/pasted into QBR slides or spreadsheets.

Metric Definitions (operationalized):
1) Latency (per-request distribution)
   - Definition: End-to-end server-sensed latency from request arrival to final token emitted (includes queueing, model decode). We report latency as percentiles: p50, p95, p99.
   - Data source: Inference service traces / Prometheus histogram metrics (inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket).
   - Units: milliseconds (ms).
   - Calculation notes: Exclude warmup / health-check traffic; align token length windows (report for short requests <=128 tokens, long requests 512-2048).
   - Example PromQL (short requests):
     sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{request_type="text", request_tokens="<=128"}[5m])) by (le)
     then compute histogram_quantile(0.95, ...).
   - Thresholds / signals for renewal: p95 > 350ms for >7 days => escalate (owner: eng-sre). p50 drift >20% post-rollout => investigate model variant or routing change.

2) Uptime / Availability
   - Definition: Percentage of successful inference requests (2xx) versus total valid requests excluding client misconfiguration (4xx). Calculated over rolling 30d and 90d windows.
   - Data source: Load-balancer logs + API gateway metrics.
   - Units: percent (0-100%).
   - SLA mapping: 99.9% = allowed max downtime ~43.8 min / month.
   - Thresholds / signals: 30d uptime < 99.5% or any single outage >10 minutes => trigger incident postmortem and notify CS. (owner: platform-ops)

3) Cost per token (effective unit economics)
   - Definition: Total billed cost attributable to inference (GPU runtime, egress, auxiliary infra) divided by total billed tokens processed (inbound+generated). Expressed as USD / 1K tokens or USD / token.
   - Data source: Billing export + token accounting (request logs aggregated per-customer).
   - Units: USD/token or USD/1K tokens (pick one and be consistent).
   - Calculation example: (gpu_hours_cost + infra_cost + storage_cost_over_period) / total_tokens_in_period.
   - Nuance: If customer uses mixed routing (cheap quantized variant + high-quality fallback), compute blended cost and separate out quality-weighted cost when discussing feature tradeoffs.
   - Thresholds / signals: Sudden >30% increase in cost/token quarter-over-quarter without corresponding quality improvement => recommend Optimize review (owner: solutions-eng + product-optimize).

4) Cache hit rate (inference cache effectiveness)
   - Definition: Percent of requests that were served from prefix/KV cache or model-level result cache vs total requests. We track: prefix-hit-rate and kv-cache-hit-rate separately.
   - Data source: runtime metrics (cache_hits / cache_lookups), request logs.
   - Units: percent (0-100%).
   - Operational notes: Include TTL semantics and hit rate per route; small overall hit rate can mask high per-template effectiveness.
   - Thresholds / signals: Route-level prefix-hit-rate < 10% for a workload expected to be cacheable => product/SE review for prompt templating. Cache hit rate collapse after deploy => likely cache key change (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Supporting signals (contextual):
- Throughput (req/s) and tokens/s to correlate cost.
- Error rate (5xx): couple with latency to detect overload.
- Model variant fallback rate: percent of requests routed to fallback model because primary exceeded capacity/failed.

Minimal KPI table (copyable CSV for slide/spreadsheet)
Headers: kpi,period,current,baseline,delta,unit,owner,notes
Rows:
latency_p50,30d,120,110,+9%,ms,eng-sre,"short-requests <=128 tokens"
latency_p95,30d,320,280,+14%,ms,eng-sre,"investigate tail after 2025-01-10 rollout"
latency_p99,30d,640,580,+10%,ms,eng-sre,"sensitive for SLAs"
uptime_30d,30d,99.72,99.9,-0.18%,%,platform-ops,"one 12m partial outage on 2024-12-22"
cost_per_1k_tokens,30d,0.82,0.60,+36%,USD/1K,finance,"blended cost including fallbacks and bursts"
cache_prefix_hit_rate,30d,18,26,-8%,%,eng-serving-runtime,"templated prompts show degradation"
kv_cache_hit_rate,30d,5,6,-1%,%,eng-serving-runtime,"low usage; consider K/V prewarm for key customers"
model_fallback_rate,30d,30,4,+650%,%,product-hosted-api,"rollout forced fallback to smaller variant due to capacity"

Actionable playbook snippets (short):
- If latency_p95 increases >25% vs baseline and uptime_30d remains >99%: open infra performance ticket, attach traces for worst 1% requests, and schedule canary rollback.
- If cost_per_1k_tokens increases >20% with cache hit rate falling >5%: coordinate SE/CS with Optimize team to evaluate batching/quantization and rework prefix templates.
- If uptime_30d < 99.5%: run incident RCA, capture customer-facing summary, propose SLA credit if covered under contract.

Person/owner mapping (recommended):
- eng-sre: latency p95/p99 investigation, platform incidents.
- eng-serving-runtime: cache behavior, KV diagnostics, model fallbacks.
- solutions-eng/product-optimize: cost/token deep-dive, batching/quantization recommendations.
- finance: billing reconciliations for effective unit cost.
- cs-manager: consolidation of KPIs for renewal QBR and customer communications.

Example queries (templates to hand to eng):
- PromQL p95 short requests: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"%ROUTE%", request_tokens=\"<=128\"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- Cache hit rate: sum(rate(cache_hits_total{route=~"%ROUTE%"}[5m])) / sum(rate(cache_lookups_total{route=~"%ROUTE%"}[5m]))
- Cost per token (SQL-ish billing export): SELECT SUM(cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(tokens),0) FROM billing WHERE customer_id = '%CUSTOMER%' AND date BETWEEN '%START%' AND '%END%';

Notes for CS-run QBRs:
- Bring the three signals: latency tail (p95/p99), uptime 30d, and cost/token. If any of these show material drift, add cache hit rate and fallback rate as explanatory metrics.
- Use the CSV KPI table above on slide 2 of the QBR deck (one-liner per KPI, baseline and delta).
- Keep remediation recommendations short and owner-assigned. If action requires infra changes, list expected customer impact window (e.g., canary rollback, capacity increase) and cost implication.

Appendix: Quick glossary
- Inbound tokens: tokens present in prompts/requests.
- Generated tokens: tokens emitted by the model.
- Blended cost: weighted average cost when multiple model variants are used for the same route.
- Prefix cache: runtime cache keyed by the beginning of a prompt/template.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing template):
- Standardize unit for cost reporting (USD/token vs USD/1K tokens). Recommendation: USD/1K tokens for external-facing slides.
- Should we include a quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/custom eval) for high-value customers to justify cost increases? Recommendation: optional column for "quality delta" if available.

Next steps:
- Get signoff from solutions-eng on calculation scripts (Devon).
- Add validated PromQL snippets to shared monitoring dashboard (Ethan).
- Pilot CSV KPI table in three QBRs and collect CS feedback (Maya).
